member.summary: The controller will be restarted. The state is saved and any changed system parameter settings will be activated after the restart.

member.summary: The main computer will be shut down. Should be used if the controller UPS is broken.

member.summary: The controller will be restarted and the Boot Application will be started. The current system is saved and deactivated (the controller is non-functional, for advanced maintenance only).

member.name: F:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Data.ControllerRestartMode.PStart
member.summary: The controller will be restarted. The current RAPID programs and data will be discarded, but not the system parameter settings.

member.name: F:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Data.ControllerRestartMode.BStart
member.summary: The controller will be restarted. The last automatically saved system state will be loaded. Should be used to recover from a system crash.

member.name: T:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Data.IoSignalSearchCriteria
member.summary:
Criteria used to search I/O signals with IoService.SearchSignals() and IoService.SearchSignalsExtended().
Every property is optional: the properties left to null are not sent to the controller, and an empty criteria matches every signal.
Two criteria can be combined by passing a second instance to the search methods, in which case a signal is returned only when it matches both. One of the two criteria should then have set to true, otherwise the result is the same as with a single criteria.

member.name: T:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Data.MastershipDomain
member.summary:
Domain of the controller a client can take the mastership of.
Mastership is what a client has to hold before it is allowed to change anything in a domain. Only one client at a time holds it, and it stays held until the client releases it or its connection ends.
The two connection versions do not cut the controller in the same domains: a connection established with version 1 keeps the configuration and the RAPID programs apart, a connection established with version 2 covers both with . Whichever name is used, the service asks the connected controller for the domains it really has.

member.name: F:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Data.MastershipDomain.Edit
member.summary:
Everything that changes the system itself: its configuration and its RAPID programs.
On a connection established with version 1, where the two are separate domains, asking for this one takes and together.

member.summary: The movement of the robot: jogging, the mechanical units and everything that makes an axis move

member.name: F:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Data.MastershipDomain.Configuration
member.summary:
The system parameters of the controller.
On a connection established with version 2, where it is not a domain of its own, this is the same domain as .

member.name: F:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Data.MastershipDomain.Rapid
member.summary:
The RAPID programs and their data.
On a connection established with version 2, where it is not a domain of its own, this is the same domain as .

member.name: T:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Internal.RwsTransportSecurity
member.summary: Prepares the process for an HTTPS connection to a robot controller.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Internal.RwsTransportSecurity.Prepare
member.summary:
Makes the process able to talk HTTPS to a robot controller.
Called on every HTTPS connection, and does nothing for a plain HTTP one, so a program that never uses HTTPS keeps the settings of its host untouched. Both steps only add what is missing, so calling it again costs two comparisons and changes nothing.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Internal.RwsTransportSecurity.EnableModernTlsProtocols
member.summary: Adds TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 to the protocols the process offers.
member.remarks: A controller only accepts TLS 1.2, while a process hosted by an executable that declares no target framework, or an old one, starts with SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0 only. The handshake then fails before any request is sent. Only the protocols are added, so a host that already chose its own set keeps it.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Internal.RwsTransportSecurity.AcceptControllerCertificate
member.summary: Accepts the certificate a controller signs itself with.
member.remarks: A controller ships a certificate no authority signed, so the default validation refuses it. Recent target frameworks say so per request, or per client, which is done where the request is built. The frameworks below cannot, and the setting of the whole process is the only place left.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.RwsException.FromHttpResponse(System.String,System.String,System.Int32,System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Builds an exception for an unsuccessful HTTP response.
The public stays generic: it names the HTTP status code and its reason phrase (Forbidden, Method Not Allowed, ...) plus a short hint about the likely cause, but never the request URL.
The carries the full diagnostics: HTTP method, full request URL, status line, the ABB error code and message read from the payload, and the raw response body.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.RwsException.FromTransportError(System.String,System.String,System.Exception)
member.summary: Builds an exception for a request that never produced an HTTP response (timeout, DNS failure, connection refused, TLS failure, ...). The public message names the failure kind only; the inner exception carries the HTTP method, the full URL and the original transport error.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.RwsException.DescribeStatusCode(System.Int32)
member.summary: Fallback reason phrase for the status codes RWS actually returns, when the transport did not give one.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.RwsException.ExplainStatusCode(System.Int32)
member.summary: Short, RWS-flavoured hint about what usually causes each status code, to point at the source of the problem.

member.name: T:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.MastershipService
member.summary:
Mastership Service - Takes and gives back the exclusive right to change a domain of the controller.
Most write operations are refused unless the client holds the mastership of the domain they belong to: moving a mechanical unit needs , changing the system parameters or the RAPID programs needs .
Only one client holds a domain at a time, and it keeps it until is called or the connection ends. Take it as late and give it back as early as possible: while it is held, the operator of the robot cannot change the same domain from the teach pendant.
Mastership belongs to the connection that took it, so every call made through the same client is the holder. None of these resources is available while the controller runs in bootserver mode.

member.summary: Gets the domains the connected controller can give the mastership of (synchronous)
member.returns: Domains the controller exposes, which are not the same on a connection established with version 1 and on one established with version 2. can be asked for on either, even when it is not listed here: it then stands for the domains covering the same ground.
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.MastershipService.GetInfo
member.summary: Gets who holds the mastership of every domain of the controller (synchronous)
member.returns: One state per domain the controller exposes, in the order it lists them
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.MastershipService.GetInfo(UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Data.MastershipDomain)
member.summary: Gets who holds the mastership of one domain (synchronous)
member.param: Domain to read the state of
member.returns: State of the domain, with telling whether this connection is allowed to write in it
member.remarks: A domain the connected controller splits in several of its own is reported as held only when every part of it is held, and the holder returned is the one of the first part somebody holds.
member.exception: Thrown when the domain is not a known one
Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed

member.exception: Thrown when the request fails, in particular when somebody else already holds one of the domains

member.remarks: In manual mode the controller only grants it once the operator has given the client the right to act on their behalf. A domain the connected controller splits in several of its own is taken as a whole: should one part be refused, the parts already taken are given back before the failure is reported.

member.name: T:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService
member.summary: System Service - Describes the system installed on the controller: its name and software version, the options and the products it was built with, the type of robot it drives, its license, and the energy it consumes. None of these resources is available while the controller runs in bootserver mode.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService.GetInfo
member.summary: Gets the name, the software version and the installed options of the system (synchronous)
member.returns: Description of the system running on the controller
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed
member.remarks: A virtual controller leaves most of the detailed version fields empty, so read them as optional. The options come along with this call, which makes unnecessary when the rest of the description is wanted too.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService.GetOptions
member.summary: Gets the options installed on the system (synchronous)
member.returns: Names of the options, in the order the controller reports them, empty when there is none
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService.GetLicense
member.summary: Gets the license the robot software runs under (synchronous)
member.returns: Name of the license, for example "VIRTUAL_USE" on a simulated controller
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService.GetRobotTypes
member.summary: Gets the type of every robot the controller drives (synchronous)
member.returns: Robot types, for example "IRB 120-3/0.6", empty when the controller drives no standard robot
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed
member.remarks: Only standard ABB robots are reported here: positioners, track motions and other mechanical units are left out, and a controller driving none of the former answers with an empty result rather than an error.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService.GetProducts(System.String)
member.summary: Gets the software products installed on the controller, with their versions (synchronous)
member.param: Name of a single product to report, null to report every installed product
member.returns: Installed products, empty when the controller reports none
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails, when is not an installed product, or when the response cannot be parsed
member.remarks: The name has to match an installed product exactly: the controller rejects an unknown one instead of answering an empty list.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService.GetEnergy
member.summary: Gets the energy the controller consumed, for the current interval and since the last reset (synchronous)
member.returns: Energy measurement, broken down per mechanical unit and per axis
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed
member.remarks: Check before reading the values: the controller answers with a complete but meaningless measurement while it has none to report.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService.GetEnergyChangeCount
member.summary: Gets the counter the controller increments each time a new energy measurement is available (synchronous)
member.returns: Current value of the counter, null when the controller did not report it
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails or the response cannot be parsed
member.remarks: This is the cheap way to poll the energy consumption: the answer is a single number, and the whole measurement only has to be read with once the counter has moved.

member.name: M:UnderAutomation.ABB.Rws.Services.SystemService.ResetAccumulatedEnergy
member.summary: Sets the accumulated energy counter of the controller back to zero (synchronous)
member.exception: Thrown when the request fails
member.remarks: The energy accumulated so far is lost: the controller keeps no history of what it counted before the reset, and the reset moment becomes the new reference reported by . The energy of the current interval is not affected.
